title: Structural and Electronic Properties of 3C/4H-SiC Interface Using Multislice Electron Ptychography
content: Silicon carbide (SiC), a wide-bandgap semiconductor, has attracted significant attention for its potential in high-power and high-temperature applications [1]. Among its various polytypes, the interface between the 3C (cubic) and 4H (hexagonal) phases is particularly noteworthy due to their distinct electronic and structural properties, including differences in bandgap [2]. Additionally, the difference in spontaneous charge polarization arising from chemical bonding can induce the formation of two-dimensional electron/hole gases (2DEGs/2DHGs), which serve as a foundation to fabricate high-electron-mobility transistors [3, 4]. The minimal lattice mismatch and fixed chemical composition at this heterojunction enable the formation of high-quality interfaces without interdiffusion [3, 4]. However, adatoms or other defects on the SiC surface during growth can introduce unintended imperfections [5], leading to performance variations. Therefore, achieving the full potential of 3C/4H-SiC heterojunctions with controlled properties necessitates a comprehensive understanding of the interface structure in relation to the growth method.
